description: Single dark-pool-anomaly signal (ratio ~3.9x baseline, kept deliberately below the historical_percentile 10M-premium bucket so this stays single-signal, not multi-signal -- an earlier draft of this fixture used a larger premium that accidentally ALSO tripped historical_percentile, making PRSX multi-signal and reaching CONFIRMED a day too early; caught by this scenario's own test and fixed by lowering the premium, not by touching any threshold), used to demonstrate a REAL multi-day lifecycle trajectory rather than a single-scan snapshot relabeled. backend/app/seed_demo_history.py backfills two real, distinct scan_date entries (today-2, today-1) into the local SQLite scan log at process startup, using this exact fixture data run through the real scan_service.evaluate_ticker_scan on each backdated day (current_state threaded forward exactly as backend/app/main.py does for a live scan) -- NOT a hardcoded state label. Day 1 (current_state=None) computes NEW. Day 2 (current_state=NEW, qualifying_days_count=1) computes BUILDING. When this ticker is then scanned live (today, via the normal /api/ticker/PRSX or /api/radar route), current_state=BUILDING and qualifying_days_count=2 are read back from that real backfilled history, and the REAL determine_transition() computes CONFIRMED via its existing 'qualifying_days_count>=2' rule -- the exact same rule a live-mode ticker would hit after two genuinely separate calendar-day scans. Known limitation, documented plainly: the named 'persistence' GATE itself (tier2_hit/is_new_qualifying_day) is still always False through backend/app/core/scan_service.py's build_gate_inputs (those two inputs are hardcoded there, unrelated to this scenario) -- this scenario demonstrates the qualifying_days_count persistence MECHANIC in determine_transition, which is what actually drives BUILDING->CONFIRMED multi-day progression in this engine, not the separately-named 'persistence' gate.
